titulo: A lot, a little, too much
intro: Quantity words change or stay the same depending on what comes after them.
p.mucho.consejo: Before a noun it changes: «mucho trabajo», «mucha gente». After a verb it does not: «trabajo mucho».
p.poco.consejo: «Poco dinero» says there is not enough; «un poco de dinero» says there is some available.
p.bastante.consejo: It does not change for gender: «bastante gente», «bastante dinero». The plural is «bastantes amigos».
p.demasiado.consejo: Before an adjective it does not change: «demasiado caro». Before a noun it does: «demasiada gente».
p.muchas.consejo: It goes with feminine plural nouns: «muchas horas», «muchas casas». The ch sounds as in «chocolate».
p.pocos.consejo: It goes with masculine plural nouns: «pocos amigos», «pocos coches». It is the opposite of «muchos».
p.la gente.consejo: In Spanish it is singular: «la gente es simpática», not «la gente son simpáticas».
p.el tiempo.consejo: It also means the weather: «hace buen tiempo». The rest of the sentence tells you which one.
p.el dinero.consejo: In everyday use it is singular: «mucho dinero», «poco dinero».
p.el ruido.consejo: The r at the start sounds strong, like «rr». The opposite of ruido is «silencio».
p.también.consejo: It adds to an affirmative sentence: «yo también trabajo». It has an accent mark: tam-BYEN.
p.tampoco.consejo: It answers a negative sentence: «No tengo tiempo» → «Yo tampoco».
b1.titulo: Three places for mucho and poco
b1.texto:
**Before a noun**, the word agrees with it: mucho trabajo, mucha gente, muchos libros, muchas horas. The same for poco, demasiado and bastante (plural: bastantes).

**After a verb**, it never changes: trabajo **mucho**, duermo **poco**, come **demasiado**.

**Before an adjective**, «very» is **muy**, never mucho: **muy** caro. Bastante and demasiado stay as they are: **demasiado** caro.

**Poco** looks at what is missing: tengo poco dinero. **Un poco de** looks at what there is: tengo un poco de dinero.

**También** adds to an affirmative sentence. **Tampoco** adds to a negative one: yo **tampoco** tengo tiempo.
b2.f0.texto: There are a lot of people in this city.
b2.f4.texto: I work a lot and I have little time.
b2.f6.texto: We have quite a few friends in the city.
b2.f7.texto: That is the best thing of all.
b4.titulo: To agree or not to agree
b4.texto:
The key is which word comes next:

- A **noun**: it agrees in gender and number: **mucha** gente, **muchos** amigos, **pocas** flores, **bastantes** libros.
- A **verb**: it does not change: trabajo **mucho**, camina **poco**.
- An **adjective**: use **muy** (muy caro), or **bastante** and **demasiado** unchanged: bastante caro, demasiado caro.

To add: **también** if the sentence is affirmative, **tampoco** if it is negative.
b4.e0.texto: There are lots of flowers in the park.
b5.titulo: A city by day and by night
b5.f0.texto: A lot of people walk along the narrow street.
b5.f1.texto: The noise of the cars fills the cold air.
b5.f2.texto: The baker hands warm bread to a lot of people.
b5.f3.texto: Few birds sing among the tall buildings.
b5.f4.texto: Time passes slowly under the yellow sun.
b5.f5.texto: A woman counts a little money on the wooden table.
b5.f6.texto: Her tired hands rest after a long day.
b5.f7.texto: The lights in the windows glow like yellow fireflies.
b5.f8.texto: The street finally keeps a soft silence.
b5.f9.texto: Many stars tremble above the dark roofs.
b6.o0.refuerzo: Yes: «gente» is feminine and singular, so it takes «mucha».
b6.o1.refuerzo: «Mucho» is masculine. «Gente» is a feminine word.
b6.o2.refuerzo: «Muchas» is plural, but «gente» is singular in Spanish.
b7.o0.refuerzo: That's it! Before an adjective you use «muy».
b7.o1.refuerzo: Before a simple adjective you do not say «mucho»: you say «muy».
b7.o2.refuerzo: «Muchos» goes with a plural noun, not with an adjective.
b7.pregunta: You say the flat costs a lot. Which sentence is correct?
b8.traduccion: I don't have much time either
b9.frase: Mi madre trabaja ____ por la tarde.
b9.o0.refuerzo: «Mucha» agrees with a noun, and after «trabaja» there is none.
b9.o1.refuerzo: «Muchos» needs a plural noun. There is no noun here.
b9.o2.refuerzo: Well done! After a verb the word does not change.
b9.pregunta: It comes after a verb. Which form do you choose?
b10.o0.refuerzo: «Poco dinero» stresses that it is little, maybe not enough.
b10.o1.refuerzo: Correct: «un poco de» presents a small but available amount.
b10.pregunta: You want to say you have some money available. Which sentence do you pick?
b12.o0.refuerzo: That says you do have a car, and you don't.
b12.o1.refuerzo: With «no» you use «tampoco»: «también» does not work in negative sentences.
b12.pregunta: Pablo has no car. Neither do you. Which sentence do you say?
b13.frase: Hay ____ ruido y no puedo dormir.
b13.o0.refuerzo: Good: «ruido» is masculine singular, so it takes «demasiado».
p.pisos.consejo: In Spain, «el piso» is a flat; it is also a floor of a building. Stress on the first syllable: «PI-sos».
p.caros.consejo: The c before a sounds «k»: «KA-ros». It agrees with «pisos». The opposite is «baratos».
p.bastantes.consejo: Plural of «bastante»: «bastantes amigos». It does not change for gender, only for number.
p.comen.consejo: From «comer», a regular -er verb: «como», «comes», «come», «comen». The c before o is hard, «k».
p.estrecha.consejo: The ch sounds as in «chocolate»: «es-TRE-cha». The opposite is «ancha». Masculine: «estrecho».
p.coches.consejo: The c before o sounds «k» and the ch is as in «chocolate»: «KO-ches». Singular: «el coche».
p.panadero.consejo: «Pan» + -ero = the person of bread: «pa-na-DE-ro». The d is soft. The woman is «panadera».
p.pájaros.consejo: The accent mark is on the first syllable and the j sounds like h: «PA-ha-ros». Singular: «pájaro».
p.cantan.consejo: From «cantar», a regular -ar verb. The c before a is hard: «KAN-tan». Birds and people both «cantan».
p.edificios.consejo: The c before i sounds «th» and «io» is one syllable: «e-di-FI-thyos». Singular: «el edificio».
p.mujer.consejo: The j sounds like h and the stress is on the end: «mu-HER». Plural: «mujeres». Also means «wife».
p.luces.consejo: Plural of «luz»: the z changes to c, «luces». The c before e sounds «th»: «LU-thes».
p.luciérnagas.consejo: The accent mark falls on «CIÉR», read «THYER»: «lu-THYER-na-gas». The g before a is hard.
p.amarillas.consejo: The ll sounds like y: «a-ma-RI-yas». It agrees with «luciérnagas», feminine plural.
p.tejados.consejo: The j sounds like h: «te-HA-dos». It comes from «teja», a roof tile. Singular: «el tejado».
p.oscuros.consejo: Stress on the middle syllable: «os-KU-ros». It agrees with «tejados». The opposite is «claros».
